title: Pressing down: Fodor's lemma and the Δ-system lemma

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 63–65 (Lemma 14.15, Definition 15.1 and Lemma 15.2; root bounds and closure function corrected)

summary: Pressing down fixes a stationary fiber and organizes uncountably many finite sets around a common root.
abstract: A function that sends each ordinal in a stationary set to a smaller ordinal must take one value on a stationary subset, provided the ambient cardinal is regular and uncountable. This pressing-down principle makes uncountably many finite sets share one common intersection while their remaining parts become disjoint. Applied to finite assignments of zeros and ones, it produces an uncountable subfamily whose members can be combined in pairs without conflicting values.
